Noncompetitive inhibitors bind to an allosteric site regardless of whether substrate is bound, so increasing substrate concentration does not reduce their effect.  
Uncompetitive inhibitors bind only to the enzyme–substrate complex, so increasing substrate concentration increases the amount of enzyme–substrate complex available for the inhibitor to bind, thereby increasing the inhibitor’s impact.  

Thus, increasing substrate concentration increases the impact of an uncompetitive inhibitor and has no effect on a noncompetitive inhibitor.  

Final answer: (C)
